signals.text: Unit 4 Musical stories Moving to music with instruction, changing movements to match the tempo, pitch or dynamics and learning that music and instruments can convey moods or represent characters.

Spring 1 South and West Africa Spring 2 Composition to represent the festival of colour (Theme: Holi festival) Learning ‘Shosholoza’ , a traditional South African song, playing the accompanying chords using tuned percussion and learning to play the djembe and some dance moves.

Summer 1 Looping and remixing Summer 2 Musical theatre Learning how dance music is created, focusing particularly on the use of loops, and learning how to play a well known song before putting a dance music spin on it to create their own versions.

They focus on the adventures of the Snail and mouse to understand how tempo can shape a musical story, Spring 1 Dynamics (Seaside) Spring 2 Sound patterns (Fairytales) Exploring the connections between music, sounds, and environments, children aim to represent the seaside.
Learning songs and creating sounds to represent three contrasting landscapes—seaside, countryside, and city—children explore how music can evoke different environments.

pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
I am so proud of our wonderful school, where, like tiny mustard seeds, our children grow from promising beginnings into successful, confident and caring individuals.
We welcome children of all faiths and none to our C of E school, which forms part of the Diocese of Gloucester Academies Trust. In partnership with parents and carers, our children develop their sense of self, their beliefs and their understanding of the world through an ambitious, knowledge-rich curriculum underpinned by Christian values of compassion, courage, forgiveness, responsibility, respect and hope.
We hope you find all the information you need on our website. We encourage you to come and experience Watermoor for yourself by arranging a visit. We are certain that you will love our school as much as we do...​​
'The vision motivates pupils to behave very well and demonstrate dignity and respect towards their peers. They are caring and support each other's wellbeing' SIAMS Report, November 2023​
‘It’s a bit like being part of a family, we’re all together in one place and we’re kind to each other’ (Y3)
​‘The teachers are compassionate; they help us if we get stuck with our learning’ (Y4)
'Staff are proud to be part of the school. They recognise the impact of their work on achieving better outcomes for children' Ofsted Report, June 2025
Get in touch
Email: officesupport@watermoor.dgat.org.uk​
The website is the hub for all news and events information.
If you would like any further information or to arrange a visit,
please contact the school office.

"The school’s Christian vision is intrinsic to the curriculum. Subject leaders plan to ensure the mustard seed approach, starting small then blossoming to flourishing, is the essence of learning. This deepens knowledge and expands thought year on year and prepares pupils for secondary school' SIAMS 2023​
At Watermoor C of E Primary School, just like mustard seeds our children grow and flourish from promising beginnings into successful, confident and capable individuals. Our curriculum is underpinned by our vision and incorporates our Christian Values of courage, respect, hope, forgiveness, compassion and responsibility. We have designed an ambitious and engaging curriculum from pre-school to Year 6, underpinned by Development Matters guidance and the National Curriculum framework, which supports children to grow and flourish in all subjects.
In response to our unique context, children explore and respond to diverse thoughts, ideas, experiences and beliefs from people and places that are different to their own, fostering a sense of being part of a global community.
We deliver a curriculum that is inclusive, accessible, and relevant to the needs and interests of our pupils.
We plan a range of immersive and engaging trips and experiences across the curriculum to enhance children’s learning, understanding and engagement.
As a Church of England school, our curriculum supports the spiritual development of our children. We use the language of ‘Ows, Wows and Nows’ to pause and reflect upon ourselves, our relationships with others and with the world in which we live.
Please see more information about each of our subjects from the Learning drop-down menu.
